suite_baseline.reconciliation: As recorded in parity/control-plane.ledger.json: 2194 collected + 5 modules skipped at collection time = 2199. Unchanged by this belt.

subsystem.name: messagebus
subsystem.note: The S8 durable-messaging belt, interlock tests/messagebus, 5 files. One ledger per source file (D-0019). The belt's whole design constraint is that it adds NO delivery store: interlock's own bus.py opens by defining itself as a thin facade that uses the S7 outbox API as found, so send / recipient-filtered poll / ack / envelope / endpoint is the entire owned surface and retry counting, delivery state transitions, lease fencing, destination dedup and ack persistence all stay in src/control_plane/outbox.ts. The single xfailed case in the whole 2,199-case source baseline lives in this belt (tests/messagebus/test_carried_specifications.py's recipient-aliasing specification).

file.note: interlock ACCEPTANCE.md item 6's 'UI attached but its session state deliberately stale', translated for C2 where there is no UI: the stale state is a provider readout that is stale or wrong. The inventory is `pytest --collect-only -q` on the source at 65f36c5, in collection order. Measured 2026-08-29 against the shared read-only clone of interlock at 65f36c5, `PYTHONPATH=src PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 -m pytest -q tests/messagebus/ -p no:cacheprovider`: 42 passed, 1 xfailed.

systematic_mappings.to: the same verbs returning a `Promise`, awaited
systematic_mappings.why: D-0301, decided by the session belt: interlock supervises children with blocking calls and uses that as a guarantee, and Node releases a child's exit status only on an event-loop turn. The stale-readout case takes the consequence rather than working around it.

systematic_mappings.from: the `provider` fixture's `yield` teardown, which stops every listed session
systematic_mappings.to: the same loop registered with `onTestFinished`, awaited
systematic_mappings.why: It runs on failure too, and it AWAITS each stop. A teardown that returns before the child is gone leaves a process holding handles inside a directory the runner is about to remove -- the child-leak hazard D-0301 retired structurally.

target_only_tests.why: None: every collected test in this file translates one source case.

entries.target_id: test/messagebus/stale-readout.test.ts::delivery is unchanged under a deliberately stale session readout > delivery is unchanged when the session's child is gone
entries.reason: Same assertion, and the strong form of it is kept: the transcript recorded with the staleness present is compared for EQUALITY with the baseline and with the expected transcript, so 'delivery outcomes are unchanged' is a comparison rather than an interpretation. The staleness is produced by a REAL child process through the S3 stub provider, not by a substituted seam -- a staleness nothing actually produced would make this a comparison of one transcript with itself. Adapted because the provider's verbs are Promise-returning here (D-0301: Node releases a child's exit status only on an event-loop turn, so interlock's blocking supervision has no equivalent), which makes the case `async` and its teardown an awaited stop rather than a signalled one. The first staleness is unchanged: start a session, stop it, and assert that the roster still answers for the id with a `providerState` beginning `exited-`.

entries.target_id: test/messagebus/stale-readout.test.ts::delivery is unchanged under a deliberately stale session readout > delivery is unchanged when the state cannot be observed
entries.reason: Same assertion, and the strong form of it is kept: the transcript recorded with the staleness present is compared for EQUALITY with the baseline and with the expected transcript, so 'delivery outcomes are unchanged' is a comparison rather than an interpretation. The staleness is produced by a REAL child process through the S3 stub provider, not by a substituted seam -- a staleness nothing actually produced would make this a comparison of one transcript with itself. Adapted because the provider's verbs are Promise-returning here (D-0301: Node releases a child's exit status only on an event-loop turn, so interlock's blocking supervision has no equivalent), which makes the case `async` and its teardown an awaited stop rather than a signalled one.
